changes: When a large TCP packet enters an IPsec tunnel, the FortiGate no longer adjusts the TCP MSS value automatically.
Update to 8.0.1 only: The configuration export commands have been restructured to give administrators explicit control over how secrets in exported configuration files are protected.
The default hostname format now includes a short serial number hash to improve device identification.
The default outbound firewall policy is no longer preconfigured on newly deployed desktop models and the FG-100F/200F series.

The override-wait-time HA setting delays a HA member with higher HA priority value from taking over as primary immediately after it boots, giving it time to synchronize sessions and prepare to process traffic before…

On FortiGate 20xG models, port1 and port2 are removed from the virtual switch and configured for DHCP by default after a factory reset or outofbox initialization to support Zero Touch Provisioning (ZTP) over these ports.
Previously, dhcpcd used an AF_PACKET socket (with BPF filter) to send and receive DHCP packets, which caused high CPU usage under heavy load.
For the FortiGate-6000 and 7000 platforms, the default HA upgrade mode has been changed to from simultaneous to uninterruptible.
The default value of udp-not-quic has changed from allow to block in both the HTTPS and DoT sub-sections of config firewall ssl-ssh-profile.
Renamed the update-server-location setting to fortiguard-server-location under config system fortiguard.
The arp-reply CLI option is now supported for IPv4 and IPv6 firewall VIPs.
Removed tenant-extraction configuration from the Inline CASB custom application CLI and GUI.
Expands the supported block size range for Port block allocation IP pools from 644096 to 164096.
The "intra-vap-privacy" setting is added for local-bridging VAP.
The default value of replacement-message has changed from disable to enable in config system automation-action when the action-type is email.
Increase extension-controller.extender size for FGT-200G and higher end to 512 to support more lan-extension connections.
The maximum length for firewall policy names has been increased from 35 to 255 characters to allow for more descriptive naming conventions.

You may be able to reduce FGCP HA failover times by changing the the NP7 link scan interval. The NP7 link scan interval is the amount of time that a FortiGate with NP7 processors waits between scans to determine if a link has failed. A shorter NP7 link scan interval can cause the FortiGate to send gratuitous ARP packets sooner after an HA failover has occurred. config system npu set np-linkscan-interval <milliseconds> end The np-link-scan-interval range is 50 to 1000ms. The default NP7 link scan interval is 1000 milliseconds (ms). If your FGCPHA cluster experiences longer than expected HA failover delays (for example a 2-second interval for a failover to occur)reducing the NP7 link scan interval may reduce HA failover delays.

On FortiGates with NP7 processors, the following new option is available to enable or disable VLAN accounting: config system npu set vlan-accounting {disable | enable} end VLAN accounting is enabled by default. VLAN accounting on a busy FortiGate with a large number of VLANs can generate large numbers of VLAN lookup (SPV/TPV) messages. In some cases these messages can cause CG-FULL conditions or packet drops, especially on very busy systems. You can use the following command to reduce the number of VLAN accounting massages that are generated by increasing the VLAN accounting interval. config system npu set vlan-acct-interval <milliseconds> end The default VLAN accounting interval is 200 milliseconds. The range is 100 to 10000 milliseconds.

Previously, dhcpcd used an AF_PACKET socket (with BPF filter) to send and receive DHCP packets, which caused high CPU usage under heavy load. Now, when dhcp-broadcast-flag is enabled (default), the L2 socket is only used to send packets when src=0, and all other DHCP traffic is handled by the L3 (UDP) socket. When dhcp-broadcast-flag is disabled, the L2 socket (ETH_P_IP) is still used for DHCP traffic, and a separate ETH_P_ARP socket handles ARP.
